clue.text: Dividing pound from fellow's working capital

indicators.note: the piece for working sits between the pound and the fellow, splitting one from the other

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound (librum)
a machine that is on is working
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: Someone describes a city's economy as separating money from the people working it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dividing' is why the working piece sits between pound and fellow; 'capital' looks like money in a financial surface, but it means a chief city.
explanation.definitionFit: The UK's seat of government is its capital city.

clue.text: Put down face up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word for face is written bottom to top

parts.note: a dial is the face of a clock or watch

explanation.surface: Instructions to lay something on a table with its front showing.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid is the past tense of lay, to set something down on a surface.

clue.text: Marriage ring like the piggy-wig's?

indicators.note: like the pig in the poem, the ring is worn inside the next word's letters

parts.note: in Lear's The Owl and the Pussy-cat, the Piggy-wig wears a ring at the end of his nose
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A wedding ring compared with the one worn by Lear's pig.
explanation.walkthrough: In Edward Lear's poem the Piggy-wig sells the ring at the end of his nose for the Owl and Pussy-cat's wedding; here the ring O goes in NOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Facetiously, wedlock is called the noose, a trap that tightens around a bachelor.

clue.text: Big event for sports college, and sound equipment's power's down

indicators.note: the power letter drops lower in the word, moving further along it

parts.note: a poly is a polytechnic, a kind of college
mics are microphones, sound equipment
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A college's sports day is ruined when the PA system loses power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' moves P from the front of POLYMICS to later in the word, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Games held every four years are the world's biggest multi-sport competition.

clue.text: Basically, here in row 15

definitions.meaning: fundamentally, when it comes down to it
row 15 is the lowest row of a 15x15 grid, the base of the puzzle

explanation.surface: A note explaining that something fundamental sits on the puzzle's last line.
explanation.definitionFit: Fundamentally is an idiomatic synonym, and the grid's last row is literally its lowest point.

clue.text: Get fitter, time drops

parts.note: rain falls in drops

explanation.surface: A fitness regime where the minutes melt away.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise regularly for fitness is a synonym sense of the verb.

clue.text: Fur upset environmental group

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset turns the word for environmental upside down

parts.note: eco- is the prefix for environmental
a lot is a group or batch

explanation.surface: Green campaigners angry about the fur trade.
explanation.definitionFit: The spotted pelt of this wild American cat is used as a fur.

clue.text: Agent finally managed second class disguise

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of agent

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: A spy who scraped by in a second-rate disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter something's appearance completely is to change it out of recognition, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Lunatic shows off behind lorry

parts.note: to moon is to show one's bare backside
a truck is a lorry

explanation.surface: A madman bares his bottom from the back of a lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' looks like a position word for the charade, but it belongs to 'shows off behind', meaning moons.
explanation.definitionFit: Being struck by the moon was once thought to cause madness, so the word means crazed.

clue.text: Effigy stuffed with vile contents lit up with shame

indicators.note: the effigy is filled with the other letters, as a guy is stuffed with rags

parts.note: a guy is an effigy of Guy Fawkes burned on Bonfire Night

indicators.note: contents means the inner letters of vile
in a down entry, up writes lit backwards, as TIL

explanation.surface: A bonfire effigy packed with something nasty is set alight, shamefully.
explanation.walkthrough: A guy is the Guy Fawkes dummy burned in Britain on 5 November; 'lit up' looks like setting it alight, but 'up' reverses 'lit' in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means in a manner showing culpability or shame.

clue.text: Pitcher's taunt having thwarted Ruth's hit?

definitions.text: Pitcher's taunt having thwarted Ruth's hit?

parts.words: Pitcher's taunt having thwarted Ruth's hit?
parts.note: a baseball pitcher who struck out Babe Ruth might crow at him, quoting a song title

explanation.surface: A baseball pitcher gloats after striking out Babe Ruth.
explanation.walkthrough: The song is Sonny and Cher's 1965 hit; 'Ruth's hit' suggests a home run, but 'hit' is the record.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous pop song title, read as a pitcher crowing at the slugger Babe Ruth.

clue.text: Back from travel after success in exam

indicators.note: the travel word comes after the exam grade

parts.note: an A is a top exam grade
to go is to travel

explanation.surface: Coming home from a trip after passing a test.
explanation.definitionFit: As in years back, meaning in the past, a time-adverb synonym.

clue.text: Large inflatable nipple burst by the German comic

parts.note: ze is the comic stage-German pronunciation of the

indicators.note: burst breaks the letters of nipple apart and reassembles them

explanation.surface: A rude comedian pops a novelty balloon.
explanation.definitionFit: The German rigid airship was a huge gas-filled dirigible.

clue.text: Services for caravan wheel in its current condition

parts.note: O is wheel-shaped
sold as is means in its present state

explanation.surface: A motorway services sells a caravan wheel without repair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Services' suggests a motorway stop and 'caravan' a towed holiday home; here the caravan is a camel train in the desert.
explanation.definitionFit: A desert watering place serves travellers crossing the sands, a witty sense of services.

clue.text: Arm policeman with soldiers blocking minor thoroughfare

indicators.note: the officer and troops stand inside the road, obstructing it

parts.note: a B-road is a minor road in Britain
DS is a detective sergeant
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Arming the police as troops close off a side road.
explanation.walkthrough: A B-road is a secondary road in the UK numbering system.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad-bladed sword is a weapon, and arm means a weapon.

clue.text: Extremely racy novel arrangement might make Austen rich

indicators.note: a new ordering of the letters of the author and her wealth

explanation.surface: Rewriting Jane Austen as erotica would make her wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' hints at Austen's books, but here means new, signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of a word meaning sexually explicit or earthy.

clue.text: 'Endless Buns': study on doughnut researchers' relaxed attitude

indicators.note: endless strips the outer letters of buns

parts.note: to con is to study
CERN, the physics lab near Geneva, runs a ring-shaped collider

explanation.surface: A scientific paper about endless buns, with doughnuts studied by lab staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A lack of worry or concern is a calm, relaxed attitude.

clue.text: Identification marks

definitions.meaning: the act of picking out or recognising something
dots or small stains on a surface

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: recognising something by sight, and a pattern of small dots.

clue.text: Wanting pair bagging a couple of Oscars?

indicators.note: the pair holds the other letters inside it, as in a bag

parts.note: O is Oscar in the NATO alphabet, so two of them

explanation.surface: Two actors greedily collecting Academy Awards.
explanation.definitionFit: Deficient or lacking, an adjective synonym, as in found wanting.

clue.text: Rider cycled here without hard seat

indicators.note: letters of rider move round from one end to the other
without drops the hard letter from here

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A cyclist with no hard saddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycled' moves the first two letters of RIDER to the end, giving DERRI; 'without' removes H from HERE, leaving ERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Seat is a polite term for the buttocks, and this French borrowing names the same.

clue.text: Main Oscar choices whittled down

indicators.note: whittled down shaves letters off both ends of the two words, leaving a run within

explanation.surface: The main nominees for the Academy Awards are narrowed to a shortlist.
explanation.definitionFit: Chief or principal, as in arch-rival, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Tease hip Republican with comedy skin piercing

indicators.note: teasing wool or hair pulls it apart, so the letters are pulled out of order

explanation.surface: A comic mocking a trendy US politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes needles that go under the skin, as in an injection.

clue.text: 'Sirrah, go' said sweet …

indicators.note: said means the words are heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: sirrah is an old contemptuous form of address to a man; to go, colloquially, is to pee

explanation.surface: An old master's command to a servant, followed into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go' here is the colloquial sense of passing water, giving PEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick with sugar, cloyingly sweet, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Outspoken bright young whippersnapper

indicators.note: outspoken means the word is spoken out, pronounced

parts.note: a sunny day is bright

explanation.surface: A clever, cheeky young person who speaks their mind.
explanation.definitionFit: A familiar way to address a young boy or upstart lad.

clue.text: Vibration limited by plane manufacturer's absorbent coat

indicators.note: the vibration is bounded on each side by the maker's letters

parts.note: BAe is British Aerospace, the aircraft maker
a throb is a pulsing vibration

explanation.surface: An aircraft maker's coating that absorbs engine shake.
explanation.walkthrough: BAe, British Aerospace (now BAE Systems), is the UK aircraft manufacturer.
explanation.definitionFit: A towelling robe worn after bathing soaks up water, a witty description of the garment.

clue.text: … old Hindu gentleman, initially blaming archaism on deficient text

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letters of blaming and archaism
deficient means the word for text is short of its final letter

parts.note: a book is a text

explanation.surface: An elderly gentleman blames old-fashioned wording on a poor text.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indian title of respect, like Mr, once used for a Hindu gentleman or clerk.

clue.text: Beeb's unending concerts, originally with Henry Wood

indicators.note: unending removes the last letter of the nickname

parts.note: the Beeb is the affectionate British nickname for the BBC

indicators.note: originally picks the first letter of concerts

parts.note: H is the symbol for henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: The BBC's Proms, founded with conductor Henry Wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wood' looks like part of Henry Wood, founder of the BBC Proms concerts, but it is the definition; the Beeb is the BBC.
explanation.definitionFit: The timber of the beech tree is a common hardwood.

clue.text: Enter Germany where 5 leaves across river

indicators.note: the Germany letter comes in to take a place in the word
the Roman five departs, making room

parts.note: over means across, as in over the road
V is the Roman numeral 5
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A train crossing a river into Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: '5' looks like a reference to 5-down (TRAIN), but it is the Roman V; D replaces it in OVER.
explanation.definitionFit: The river forming much of the border between Germany and Poland.

clue.text: Source of iron rule in strictly secular school?

parts.note: the rule on religion in a strictly secular place is none at all, O for nil
RE, religious education, is a school subject in Britain

explanation.surface: The rule about religion in a firmly non-religious school.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is religious education, compulsory in British schools; the rule in a wholly secular one would be none of it, nil RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron is smelted from rock containing the metal.

clue.text: Story of modern life in England: Uber all over the place

indicators.note: all over the place means scattered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Ride-hailing cars are now everywhere in England.
explanation.definitionFit: A contemporary folk tale, often spread as true, about modern life.

clue.text: 1a (19 only) caught by anybody playing Irish anthem

indicators.note: the jumbled letters hold the single letter, as in a catch
playing means the letters of anybody are in play, rearranged
19-down means the backside or bottom, so only the bottom letter of the city

parts.note: 1-across is the capital city

explanation.surface: Londonderry's tune, played by anyone, is Ireland's song.
explanation.walkthrough: 1a and 19 together give Londonderry: the song is sung to the Londonderry Air. Here '19 only' takes just the bottom of 1a, its final N.
explanation.definitionFit: The ballad sung to the Londonderry Air is an unofficial anthem for the Irish.

clue.text: Chap engaged in ogling? Not half

definitions.text: Chap engaged in ogling? Not half

indicators.note: the short man sits inside the ogling word, engaged within it

parts.note: to leer is to ogle

indicators.note: not half means keep only one half of chap, its front two letters

explanation.surface: Is that man ogling? Not half he is!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'very much so', which makes the whole clue the definition as well as the halving signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A man given to lustful staring and pestering fits the whole clue's picture.
